<jats:title>A<jats:sc>bstract</jats:sc>
                     </jats:title><jats:p>We describe a class of holographic models that may describe the physics of certain four-dimensional big-bang/big-crunch cosmologies. The construction involves a pair of 3D Euclidean holographic CFTs each on a homogeneous and isotropic space <jats:italic>M</jats:italic> coupled at either end of an interval ℐ to a Euclidean 4D CFT on <jats:italic>M ×</jats:italic> ℐ with many fewer local degrees of freedom. We argue that in some cases, when the size of <jats:italic>M</jats:italic> is much greater than the length of ℐ, the theory flows to a confining three-dimensional field theory on <jats:italic>M</jats:italic> in the infrared, and this is reflected in the dual description by the asymptotically AdS spacetimes dual to the two 3D CFTs joining up in the IR to give a Euclidean wormhole. The Euclidean construction can be reinterpreted as generating a state of the Lorentzian 4D CFT on <jats:italic>M ×</jats:italic> time whose dual includes the physics of a big-bang/big-crunch cosmology. When <jats:italic>M</jats:italic> is ℝ<jats:sup>3</jats:sup>, we can alternatively analytically continue one of the ℝ<jats:sup>3</jats:sup> directions to get an eternally traversable four-dimensional planar wormhole. We suggest explicit microscopic examples where the 4D CFT is <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:tex-math>$$ \mathcal{N} $$</jats:tex-math><mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                  <mml:mi>N</mml:mi>
                </mml:math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula> = 4 SYM theory and the 3D CFTs are superconformal field theories with opposite orientation. In this case, the two geometries dual to the pair of 3D SCFTs can be understood as a geometrical version of a brane-antibrane pair, and the tendency of the geometries to connect up is related to the standard instability of brane-antibrane systems.</jats:p>
title: Cosmology from confinement?
